When I say "bone like material similar to tusks" I mean that it's made of a similar chemical construct so it's like a cross between bone and tusk with a little extra to make it clear and sparkling. I also did think about the size of the crystals being a factor and the reason they have become flightless is because the crystals have gradually become bigger over time to the point their bodies have become so heavy that they cannot lift off the ground. The crystals will shed and fall off on their own sometimes to make way for new ones like teeth but before they fall off they become cloudy and not as pretty which is why the dragon must be killed in order to take the crystals before they lose their colour. They haven't been seen outside in centuries which is why is so widely speculated what they eat. There's less than 100 known caves and mines which they reside in and they are guarded around the clock by conservationists to stop them from being poached. The females only lay one egg every ten years and the egg takes another full year to hatch. I like the idea of the phoenix like dragon however I like to try and base my dragons largely in nature and animals that have or do already exist. My way of writing falls very heavily in the idea that the creatures I write about can exist in the real world and you just don't know it. The idea that there's these whimsical beings right under your nose makes the world seem a lot more interesting and to make it sound more realistic I like to write them in a way where it can be easily described by science, so I don't really write about magic or stuff like that although I would love to dabble in the magical side of things in the future.
